top news.title: Microsoft's Xbox unit plans to cut 3,200 jobs over the next year, including 1,600 on Monday, and divest up to five studios, including Ninja Theory, in a “reset”

tweets.author: @asha_shar
tweets.text: This is an important email I sent today to all employees at XBOX: Team, We are beginning the most significant restructure in XBOX history.  After careful consideration, I've made the difficult decision to reduce our team by approximately 3,200 throughout FY27.  This will include approximately 1,600 role eliminations today, and in addition, four studios will leave XBOX to new management.

tweets.author: @stephentotilo
tweets.text: Four studios being divested (Compulsion, Undead Labs, DoubleFine, Ninja Theory) account for around 350 of the job cuts, I'm told. Arkane could add 100+ more While the fate of those studios will draw a lot of attention, the lion's share of the 3,200 cuts are outside those teams

tweets.author: @paultassi
tweets.text: I think the main problem with Xbox going forward is going to be what's not addressed in today's announcement, that it has to turn around its core console business and there is still no coherent path to do so.  That is arguably its most important strategy component now (expanding console adoption is the biggest potential way to expand Game Pass), which comes after two bad generations, unlike its competitors also dealing with hardware issues.

sub_items.title: Microsoft is laying off ~4,800 employees, or ~2.1% of its workforce; most are in sales or Xbox, where ~20% of jobs are set to be cut by the end of FY 2027

top news.title: Broadcom agrees to expand its Apple partnership through 2031 to develop and supply custom chips; in 2023, the companies announced a multibillion-dollar 5G deal

tweets.author: @markgurman
tweets.text: Apple and Broadcom have announced an extended partnership that runs through 2031. All signs point to this being related to Apple's first chips developed specifically for AI servers.

tweets.author: @aktiehedonist
tweets.text: Apple is around 20% of Broadcom revenue, and despite designing more silicon in-house, they still rely on Broadcom for key wireless/RF/connectivity components.  To me this is another reminder of the Broadcom model: get deeply embedded with the most demanding customers, then stay there for multiple generations.
